subject: Outbound access & IP permitlist for BlueLake private deployment
messages:
From: Alex Taylor <alex.taylor@bluelake.ai>
To: jasmine.liu@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 4 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Outbound access and permitlist for Redwood Private (BlueLake)

Hi Jasmine,

We're preparing the network changes for our upcoming Redwood Private deployment in our on-prem DC. Security wants a concise list of what we need to allow through our firewall/NAT for the control plane and model telemetry. Specific asks:

- Exact FQDNs and minimal ports required (we want to avoid broad 0.0.0.0/0 egress rules).
- Whether Redwood needs persistent egress IP(s) or if hostname-based allowlisting behind a forward proxy is OK.
- Any TLS inspection / mutual-TLS requirements (we run a corporate TLS proxy by default).
- Sample firewall policy text or a one-page runbook we can hand to infra.

Can you send over an IP/FQDN permitlist and any constraints we should plan for? I've attached our internal template (see later).

Thanks,
Alex Taylor
Security Engineer, BlueLake Systems
security@bluelake.ai
[Attachment: bluelake_ip_matrix.csv (text/csv)]

From: jasmine.liu@redwood.ai <jasmine.liu@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Taylor <alex.taylor@bluelake.ai>
Cc: hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 4 May 2027 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Outbound access and permitlist for Redwood Private (BlueLake)

Hi Alex — thanks for the clear checklist. High-level guidance below; I attached two artifacts: a concise firewall policy excerpt and a permit matrix we maintain for Private installs.

Summary (short):
- Preferred: Provision a small set of static NAT egress IPs (1-3) for control-plane and telemetry => easiest for compliance.
- Acceptable alternative: Allow outbound by FQDN via your forward proxy (must not terminate TLS if you require Redwood to authenticate the client cert).
- Required outbound destinations (FQDNs):
  * controlplane.redwood.ai:443 (API registration, health checks, rollout control)
  * telemetry.redwood.ai:443 (aggregated usage/health events)
  * models-cdn.redwood.ai:443 (model fetches during upgrades; may be CDN fronted)
  * auth.redwood.ai:443 (token exchange and signing)
- Ports: 443 outbound only. No inbound ports required to our service from your network.
- TLS: TLS 1.2+ required; we do not support enterprise TLS interception for control-plane auth if interception breaks client cert chains. If you must inspect, configure bypass for the above FQDNs or use TLS passthrough.

Operational notes:
- Model downloads are sometimes served from large CDN ranges; FQDN allowlisting at the proxy is more future-proof than maintaining huge IP lists.
- If you need static IPs for audit whitelists, we can reserve a small NAT IP set for you and publish them in the runbook; these IPs will be used for control/telemetry but not for customer model payloads when using on-prem model cache (call out in runbook).

I attached: redwood_fw_policy_excerpt.txt (one-page firewall rules you can paste) and bluelake_ip_matrix.csv (mapping of FQDN->purpose).

Next steps: if you confirm "static NAT" vs "FQDN-proxy" we'll send a one-page pre-deploy runbook for your infra team and a short test plan.

-jasmine
Jasmine Liu
Integration Lead, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: redwood_fw_policy_excerpt.txt (text/plain)]

From: jasmine.liu@redwood.ai <jasmine.liu@redwood.ai>
To: dev.patel@redwood.ai
Cc: hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 4 May 2027 10:09:00 -07:00
Subject: FW: Outbound access and permitlist for BlueLake private deployment — engineering confirm

Dev — looping you in for engineering confirmation on a couple of points before I send the runbook to BlueLake:

1) For control-plane and telemetry, can we guarantee traffic originates from a stable small set of egress IPs (confirm ranges) when using Private in their VPC/edge stack?
2) Are there any additional outbound ports/protocols (websockets, gRPC long-poll) that their firewall should permit beyond 443?
3) Recommend text for the runbook about FQDN vs IP allowlist tradeoffs.

I've attached our internal egress matrix (internal_egress_matrix.xlsx) — helps map which service talks where. Can you reply with the preferred-ip-blocks.txt attached and a short bullet approval? We need this today to keep their schedule.

Thanks — jasmine

From: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>
To: jasmine.liu@redwood.ai
Cc: hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 4 May 2027 14:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: FW: Outbound access and permitlist for BlueLake private deployment — engineering confirm

Jasmine — quick answers (engineer notes):

1) Static egress IPs: yes, for Private we can push control-plane/telemetry traffic over a NAT gateway with a small set of static IPs. See attached preferred-ip-blocks.txt (we propose 3 addresses for redundancy).

2) Ports/protocols: outbound only TCP/443 is sufficient. We open web-sockets over TLS on the same 443 port for live-control channels; no additional ephemeral ports required. No SSH/RDP egress.

3) Runbook guidance: use FQDN allowlist at your forward proxy for CDN/model fetches (CDN IPs change frequently). For control-plane and telemetry, prefer IP-based allowlist + a note that IPs are owned by Redwood and will only be used for control/telemetry. Also include a fallback section: if the proxy does TLS inspection, configure passthrough for controlplane.redwood.ai and auth.redwood.ai or provide a short mTLS configuration (we support mTLS for enterprise on request).

Attaching the small IP list and patch text. Approve to send to BlueLake.

— Dev
(Attachment: preferred-ip-blocks.txt)

From: Alex Taylor <alex.taylor@bluelake.ai>
To: jasmine.liu@redwood.ai
Cc: security@bluelake.ai
Date: Wed, 5 May 2027 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Outbound access and permitlist for BlueLake private deployment

Jasmine / team — this is excellent, thank you. Our plan:

- We'll provision a NAT gateway with three static egress IPs and add the 443-only rule to the firewall for those IPs.
- For model fetches we'll route through our forward proxy by FQDN (model CDN traffic), but we will exempt the controlplane/auth endpoints from TLS termination (passthrough).
- I'll open NET-1284 in our Jira with the runbook attached and target the infra change window next Thursday (2027-05-13).

Please send the one-page pre-deploy runbook and a short validation checklist (smoke tests) and we'll slot it in.

Thanks — Alex
Alex Taylor
Security Engineer, BlueLake Systems
